learn: The beat is the steady pulse that keeps going, like a clock: tick, tick, tick.
Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds in the words or tune.
You can tap the beat with your foot and clap the rhythm with your hands.
check: The pattern of long and short sounds
Can you tap the beat and clap the rhythm?
lessons.try: Sing "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star". Tap the beat, then clap the words.

learn: Rhythm patterns can be short and repeat.
Say "pizza, pizza, apple pie": the syllables make a rhythm.
Musicians copy and create rhythm patterns.
check: What makes rhythm in "pizza, pizza, apple pie"?
lessons.try: Make up a rhythm with the names of three foods.

learn: Body percussion uses your body as a drum.
You can stomp, pat your knees, clap and snap.
Put sounds together to make a pattern: stomp, pat, clap, rest.
check: Using your body to make rhythm
A rest in your pattern means...
lessons.try: Make a four-beat body percussion pattern and repeat it.

learn: Music can be written down with notes.
A quarter note has a filled-in head and a stem. It lasts one beat.
We can say "ta" for a quarter note.
check: How long does a quarter note last?
What do we say for a quarter note?
A quarter note has a filled-in head and a...
lessons.try: Clap four quarter notes while saying "ta, ta, ta, ta".

learn: Two eighth notes are joined by a beam. Together they last one beat.
We say "ti-ti" for two eighth notes.
They sound quicker than a quarter note.
check: What do we say for two eighth notes?
lessons.try: Clap "ta, ti-ti, ta, ti-ti".

learn: A quarter rest means one beat of silence.
We can whisper "shh" or open our hands for a rest.
Rests are as important as notes.
check: What can you whisper for a rest?
lessons.try: Clap "ta, ta, shh, ta".

learn: A melody is a tune: notes that go up, down and stay the same, one after another.
When you hum a song, you are humming the melody.
Melodies can be happy, sad, calm or exciting.
check: When you hum a song, you hum the...
lessons.try: Hum the melody of a song you love.

learn: A melody can move by step, going to the very next note.
It can skip, jumping over notes.
It can repeat the same note.
check: Moving to the very next note is a...
Can a melody repeat a note?
lessons.try: Sing "do, re, mi" (steps), then "do, mi, sol" (skips).

learn: Move your hand up when the melody goes up.
Move your hand down when it goes down.
Keep it level when the note repeats.
check: When the melody goes up, your hand goes...
When the note repeats, your hand...
Showing melody with hands helps you...
lessons.try: Sing "Mary Had a Little Lamb" and move your hand with the melody.

learn: Sol and mi are two notes. Sol is higher. Mi is lower.
Many playground songs use just sol and mi, like "Rain, rain, go away".
Singers use hand signs to show the notes.
check: Which song uses sol and mi?
What do singers use to show notes?
lessons.try: Sing "sol, mi, sol, mi" up and down.

learn: For sol, hold your hand flat, palm facing you, at chest height.
For mi, hold your hand flat, palm down, a little lower.
Hand signs help you see high and low.
check: Where is the sol hand sign?
lessons.try: Do the hand signs while singing "sol, mi, sol, sol, mi".

learn: La is just above sol.
Sol, mi and la make lots of children's songs.
Listen and decide: is this note sol, mi or la?
check: Which notes make many children's songs?
Which is the highest of these: mi, sol, la?
lessons.try: Sing "sol, la, sol, mi" with hand signs.

learn: Dynamics means how loud or soft music is.
Forte (f) means loud. Piano (p) means soft.
Musicians read these letters in written music.
check: What does f stand for in music?
How loud or soft music is
lessons.try: Sing a song once forte and once piano.

learn: Crescendo means getting louder little by little.
Decrescendo means getting softer little by little.
These changes make music exciting.
check: A storm coming and going could be...
lessons.try: Pretend a storm is coming: drum softly, then louder, then softer as it leaves.

learn: Composers choose dynamics to match the feeling.
A lullaby is usually soft. A march is often loud.
You can choose dynamics when you perform.
lessons.try: Decide which dynamics fit a song about a sleeping baby.

learn: Tempo is the speed of the beat.
Allegro means fast. Largo means very slow.
The tempo changes how music feels.
lessons.try: March to a fast song and sway to a slow one.

learn: Accelerando means getting faster.
Ritardando means getting slower.
Many songs slow down at the very end.
lessons.try: Clap a steady beat, then speed up, then slow down.

learn: Tempo can tell us how to move: fast music for running, slow music for tiptoeing.
Animals move at different tempos: a snail is slow, a mouse is quick.
Composers write music to sound like moving animals.
check: Can music sound like moving animals?
lessons.try: Move like an elephant to slow music and like a bird to fast music.

learn: String instruments make sound when strings vibrate.
Violins, violas, cellos and basses are bowed. Guitars and harps are plucked.
The bigger the instrument, the lower its sound.
check: How do string instruments make sound?
Which is lower: violin or cello?
lessons.try: Listen to a violin and a cello. Which is lower?

learn: Woodwinds make sound when air is blown across or through them. Flutes, clarinets and oboes are woodwinds.
Brass instruments make sound when players buzz their lips. Trumpets, trombones and tubas are brass.
The tuba is the biggest and lowest brass instrument.
lessons.try: Buzz your lips like a trumpet player.

learn: Percussion instruments are hit, shaken or scraped: drums, cymbals, xylophones, maracas.
An orchestra is a big group with all four families.
A conductor leads the orchestra.
lessons.try: Make a pretend orchestra with family members, each playing a different family.

learn: Songs are made of parts, or sections.
Musicians label sections with letters: A, B, C.
If a section repeats, it gets the same letter.
check: What are sections of a song?
If a section repeats, it gets...
lessons.try: Listen to a song and raise your hand when a part repeats.

learn: AB form has two different sections: A, then B.
The A part might be smooth and the B part bouncy.
Move one way for A and another way for B.
check: AB form has how many different sections?
In AB form, which comes first?
How can you show AB form?
lessons.try: Sway for A and hop for B as you listen to a song.

lessons.t: ABA Form and Verse and Chorus
learn: ABA form goes A, B, then A again. It is like a sandwich.
Many songs have verses and a chorus. The verse words change. The chorus words repeat.
Knowing the form helps you remember a song.
check: Which part of a song repeats the same words?
lessons.try: Find the chorus in a song you know.

learn: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Feet flat on the floor, chin level.
Good posture gives your breath room.
check: How should you stand to sing?
lessons.try: Stand tall like a puppet with a string on your head and sing a note.

learn: Breathe in through your nose, filling your belly like a balloon.
Let the air out slowly while you sing.
Do not lift your shoulders when you breathe in.
check: How do you let air out when singing?
lessons.try: Breathe in for four counts, then hiss out for eight counts.

learn: Singing in tune means matching the notes you hear.
Listen first, then sing back.
Use a gentle singing voice, not a shout.
check: What does singing in tune mean?
lessons.try: A grown-up sings a note. You match it.

learn: Every culture in the world has music.
People sing at celebrations, while working and to put babies to sleep.
Music helps people share stories and feelings.
lessons.try: Ask a family member what songs they sang as a child.

learn: The sitar is a string instrument from India.
The djembe is a drum from West Africa, played with the hands.
The didgeridoo is a long wooden wind instrument made by Aboriginal Australians.
check: The djembe is a drum from...
lessons.try: Listen to a recording of a djembe and play the rhythm on a box.

learn: Folk songs are old songs passed down through families.
Many folk songs come with dances, like circle dances.
When we learn songs from other places, we respect the people who made them.
check: When we learn songs from other places, we...
Respect the people who made them
lessons.try: Learn a simple circle dance with your family.
